standard_prerequisites.name: Definiteness of the Chern classes after an envelope and existence of resolutions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-chern-classes-defined, invoked at proof line 9480; Derived Categories of Schemes, label perfect-proposition-perfect-resolution-property, invoked at proof line 9487
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces, when the irreducible components of X are quasi-compact, an envelope Y -> X splitting into quasi-compact pieces with the resolution property, so that condition (3) implies condition (1).

core_obligations: Assume condition (1): choose an envelope f : Y -> X and a map of locally bounded complexes alpha representing Lf^*E_1 -> Lf^*E_2. The cone C(alpha) is locally bounded and finite locally free because C(alpha)^n = E_2^n direct sum E_1^{n+1}, and it represents Lf^*E_3, so all three Chern classes are defined; since c_p is characterised by restriction to Y it suffices to prove c(E_2) = c(E_1) c(C(alpha)) in the product over A^p(Y) (proof lines 9451-9466).

Reduce further to bounded complexes of fixed rank by restricting to a connected component of Y, where the desired equality is exactly the multiplicativity statement for a short exact sequence of finite locally free modules; the cases of ch and P_p are handled by the corresponding additivity lemma (proof lines 9467-9474).

Dispose of the remaining conditions: condition (2) implies (1) because a map of complexes on X base changes to one on Y; if the irreducible components of X are quasi-compact, argue as in the definiteness lemma to find an envelope Y -> X with Y a disjoint union of quasi-compact schemes each having the resolution property, restrict the map to each Y_i and represent it by a map of bounded complexes of finite locally free modules, so that condition (3) implies (1); condition (4) implies (3) and the proof is complete (proof lines 9476-9490).
proof_roadmap: Handle condition (1) by taking the cone of a representing map and restricting to a connected component (proof lines 9451-9474).
Observe that condition (2) implies condition (1) (proof lines 9476-9479).
Use the envelope with the resolution property to show condition (3), hence condition (4), also reduces to condition (1) (proof lines 9479-9490).
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the additivity of the total Chern class, the Chern character and the Chern polynomials along a distinguished triangle of perfect objects under any of four increasingly weak hypotheses on X, from the existence of a representing map of complexes after an envelope up to quasi-compactness of X (statement lines 9426-9448, tag 0F9F). The proof must first see that the cone of the representing map is again a locally bounded complex of finite locally free modules, which is what makes all three classes defined, then reduce to a connected component so that the multiplicativity lemma applies, and finally show that the weaker hypotheses imply the first by finding an envelope over which resolutions exist. The reduction through the hypotheses is the substance, so the claim is H2.
